title: Resurrection and Redemption
english: The resurrection of Lazarus demonstrates God's power to raise even the foreign nations, as it shows that He will raise all humanity, which is composed of four elements and is subject to sin, impurity, and domination by evil forces, even if it stinks in the sin of transgression, even if it rots in the impiety of idolatry, and even if it is dominated by demons and dragged to their will, as well as being dominated by worms.

The angels and humans who witnessed the resurrection of Lazarus were amazed and began to shout and praise God, saying 'Hosanna in the highest, blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, Hosanna in the highest' (Matthew 21:9), which is not only a recognition of Jesus as a sign-bearer but also as a king who has triumphed over the forces of evil.

The prophet Zechariah invites all who love the kingdom of the Lord to hear his words, for he has been granted the privilege of nourishing us in this feast, as the Lord says, 'Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word proceeding from the mouth of God' (Matthew 4:4).

Zechariah cries out with joy, saying, 'Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion' (Zechariah 9:9), because the one who will restore you has come, and this is in accordance with the announcement made by the father of the king who will restore you, who said, 'When the Lord restored the captivity of Zion, we were like those who dream. Then our mouth was filled with joy and our tongue with shouts of triumph.'

The daughter of Zion is called to return from the captivity of demons and the exile of this age to the Jerusalem above, which Abraham awaited, as the blessed apostle Paul says, 'You have approached Mount Zion and the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and myriads of angels, a festive gathering and the church of the firstborn who are enrolled in heaven, and God the judge of all and the spirits of the righteous made perfect' (Hebrews 12:22-23).

As a result, pain, sorrow, and sighing have fled, and all the righteous rejoice in their dwelling place, and so it is time to rejoice and be glad, and to greatly rejoice, O daughter of Zion, because the terrible one will no longer take you captive, and the one who redeems you is not like other kings, but an eternal king with an eternal kingdom, as the angel Gabriel announced to the virgin Mary, 'And of his kingdom, there will be no end' (Luke 1:33).

Through this, you are called to rejoice greatly and to proclaim the good news to your king, who came down from heaven to save you, with thanksgiving, praise, and hymnology, saying 'Hosanna in the highest, from where you came to save me, blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord' (Matthew 21:9), for the kingdom of our father is indeed blessed as it comes.

As the prophet Zechariah preaches the gospel, running ahead of the kingdom a long time before, we are to hear and understand what he says, and to enjoy, as rational beings, the words proceeding from the mouth of God through him.

The prophet Zechariah also says, 'They will be intoxicated from the drinking of your house' (Psalm 36:8), and we are to come and hear what he prophesies about the kingdom of the Lord, and to nourish our souls with the divine teachings.

For the Lord says, 'They will be intoxicated from the drinking of your house' (Psalm 36:8), and we are to come and enjoy the words proceeding from the mouth of God, and to nourish our souls with the divine teachings, and to proclaim, 'Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father'.
The evangelist proclaims Christ twice, first as the one who comes in the highest, indicating his divine nature, and then as the one who comes in the name of the Lord, indicating his human nature.

For the coming kingdom of our father is indeed blessed, for the coming kingdom of our father is blessed, as it signifies the blessed seed by which Abraham was blessed, and through which all nations of the earth were blessed in his seed (Genesis 22:18).

The translation aims to preserve the original word order and meaning as much as possible, while still conveying the author's intended message in natural literary prose.

title: Rejoice Daughter of Zion
english: Let us take up the former voice once more and seize a prophetic breast, for it still has milk and good visions.
For it says, 'Rejoice exceedingly, daughter of Zion; cry out, daughter of Jerusalem'.

The prophet cries out with this distinction, and we must pay close attention to it, because the names of plants, birds, quadrupeds, and humans all have different forms and powers, and similarly, each horn of the divine sayings has its own unique power and vision.
We need to investigate why the prophet first calls the faithful Jerusalem 'daughter of Zion' and then 'daughter of Jerusalem'.

The answer lies in the meaning of Zion, which is interpreted as 'thirsty', referring to the synagogue of the righteous and prophets who, the prophets, who from eternity until the coming of Christ thirsted to be united and pleasing to the divine and worshipful substance of the deity, as the chief of the apostles Peter says, 'So that they may become partakers of the divine nature'.

These individuals, who sought the Lord and thirsted for Him, were called Zion, and when they finally attained their goal and saw God's face, they became Jerusalem, the city that sees God and is the watchtower of all knowledge.

The daughter of Zion calls the faithful in the Lord, those who thirst through faith and seek through the work of the gospel's commandments to find the Lord, the one hidden in them, as the Holy Spirit says, 'This is the generation that seeks the Lord, seeking the face of the God of Jacob'.
When they attain their goal, they are called the daughter of the aforementioned Jerusalem, for they behold God and contemplate spiritual knowledge.
The prophet, exhorting God through the Spirit, asks Him to reveal this Zion and Jerusalem, saying, 'Remember your assembly, which you acquired from the beginning'.

Then, crying out with the mother, Zion, 'Rejoice exceedingly, daughter of Zion; proclaim, daughter of Jerusalem', they cry out heavenly, 'Hosanna in the highest, blessed is the one coming in the name of the Lord'.
The gospel says, 'When they approached Jerusalem and came to Bethphage'.
Jesus sent two of his disciples, who are two groups of prophets and apostles, to the mount of Olives, which is the faithful church from the people.
For he sent them to all the inhabited world of the nations, because they were previously opposed to the faithful church from the people.
For at a suitable time he sent them to the village opposite of the nations. For it was ready to receive the previously mentioned two choirs of apostles and prophets.
And to bring to him the colt, which are the nations, to mount and reign over them, as the psalmist says, 'The Lord reigns over the nations, the Lord sits on his holy throne'.
On which no human has ever sat. For neither is God mounting and reigning over them, nor law nor prophets.

Having loosed him, he says, bring him to me. For the apostles loosed the nations from darkness, that is, from ignorance of God, from error, from sin, from foreign slavery, from the power of darkness, from the ruler of this age. And they brought them to their creator and lord.
And behold, he sits on them and reigns as on the cherubim, crying out and saying, 'Hosanna in the highest, blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord'.

Peace on earth and glory in the highest. For Luke says so. Peace on earth, why does he say this? Did the angels not have peace on earth? Yes, and they had peace within themselves, the peace that surpasses all understanding, as the wise Paul says. They had peace in heaven, but not with humans. The heaven had peace in itself.
When the angels saw this, …
The prophet says, 'Rejoice exceedingly, daughter of Zion; cry out, daughter of Jerusalem', and this is a call to the faithful to rejoice and cry out, for the Lord is coming.
The gospel says, 'When they approached Jerusalem and came to Bethphage', and this is a fulfillment of the prophecy.
And Jesus sent two of his disciples to the mount of Olives, which is the faithful church from the people, to bring to him the colt, which are the nations, so that he could mount and reign over them.
And the psalmist says, 'The Lord reigns over the nations, the Lord sits on his holy throne', and this is a declaration of the Lord's reign over the nations.

And the apostles loosed the nations from darkness, and brought them to their creator and lord, and behold, he sits on them and reigns as on the cherubim, crying out and saying, 'Hosanna in the highest, blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord'.
And then it says, 'Peace on earth and glory in the highest', and this is a declaration of peace and glory.
And when the angels saw this, they had peace within themselves, but not with humans, and the heaven had peace in itself, and then they said…

title: The Triumphal Entry
english: As angels rouse all humanity through the sign of Lazarus, and heaven and humanity are at peace, and they cry out in unison, saying: 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, peace on earth and glory in the highest' (Matthew 21:9).
They put garments on the foal, which signifies the grace given to the nations, and through this grace they mounted Jesus upon it, and by their own virtues (καὶ διὰ τὰς ἰδίας ἀρετάς).
Additionally, they are praised for their own virtues, which they have yoked to grace, as is evident when others spread their garments on the road (Matthew 21:8).

According to the divine Paul, having been justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we also have access by faith to this grace, in which we stand, and we boast in hope of the glory of God (Romans 5:1-2).

Furthermore, we boast in our tribulations, knowing that tribulation produces endurance, and endurance produces proven character, and proven character produces hope, and this hope does not disappoint, because the love of God has been poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit who has been given to us (Romans 5:3-5).

The crowds that preceded and followed him cried out with praises and olive and palm branches, which signify the practical work of the outer man, and palm branches, which signify the spiritual and practical and pure work of the inner man, and they cried out saying: 'Hosanna in the highest' (Matthew 21:9).

In truth, all the crowds of the righteous and prophets and priests, who are those preceding and following, cry out and say with faith: 'Hosanna to the son of David; blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord; Hosanna in the highest' (Matthew 21:9).

As the evangelist says, all this happened that the word spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying 'Tell the daughter of Zion' (Matthew 21:5); the prophet says that he desired to see and hear, not he alone but also many prophets and righteous ones.

The prophet says to tell the daughter of Zion that her king is coming to her, and he says 'he is coming to you', that is, to be yours and to dwell in you, righteous and saving, saving from the slavery of the enemy those who believe in him (Matthew 21:5, Zechariah 9:9).

He is gentle and mounted on a donkey, a colt, the son of a beast of burden, and in his humility, he destroys the chariots of the kingdom of Ephraim, which represents the devil's rule over Israel and the nations; until Christ came, the anointing and the kingdom of the Jews came and ceased.
Through his humble donkey, the pride of their authority is destroyed, which is from Jerusalem.

The patriarch Jacob blesses Judah and shows that the blessing is directed towards his fathers Abraham and Isaac, which ultimately points to Christ; Jacob says that he ties his donkey to a vine, so that the unclean nations may receive from it the law and the prophets, and ultimately receive Christ, who is the blessing of the nations and their purification.

Jacob also says that the donkey is tied to the vine, which is a symbol of Christ, who sprouted from the vine of the synagogue that came from Egypt, as indicated by the phrase 'from a shoot' (Genesis 49:11).
